"""cnp-and-dline-calibration on gatemap run 5: per-row ridge extraction (two ridges), ratio fit on the
operating window near D = 0, offsets, closure check, realized D = 0 n-window; writes cal params to JSON."""
import json
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages

rid = 5
g = fan_grids(str(Path(file_path) / str(rid))); rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"]); Vbg = g.slow
fs = g.meta["fast_setpoints"]; Vtg = np.asarray(fs[0] if isinstance(fs[0], list) else fs)
c_tg0 = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg0 = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])
print(f"run {rid}: {g.nrows} rows x {g.nfast}; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; prior c_bg/c_tg = {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}")

# ridge extraction: per row, up to two peaks; track continuity from the high-|D| end where ridge A is unambiguous
pts = []   # (Vbg, Vtg, R, ridge)
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.05 * (r.max() - r.min()) + 5)
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]:
        pts.append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))
pts = np.array(pts)
# assign to ridges by distance to the high-D fit of ridge A (rows Vbg < -0.6), then refit each
selA = pts[:, 0] < -0.6
cfA0 = np.polyfit(pts[selA, 0], pts[selA, 1], 1)
dist = pts[:, 1] - np.polyval(cfA0, pts[:, 0])
ridgeA = pts[np.abs(dist) < 0.08]; ridgeB = pts[(dist < -0.08) & (dist > -0.45)]

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    print(f"{label}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vbg [{lo:+.2f},{hi:+.2f}]: Vtg = {cf[0]:+.4f} Vbg {cf[1]:+.4f}; "
          f"c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; rms {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV")
    return cf

print("--- ridge A (main) ---")
cfA_all = fit(ridgeA, -2, 2, "A all rows")
cfA_hiD = fit(ridgeA, -2, -0.6, "A high-D rows")
cfA_op = fit(ridgeA, -0.5, 0.5, "A operating window |Vbg|<0.5")
print("--- ridge B (parallel, lower Vtg) ---")
cfB_all = fit(ridgeB, -2, 2, "B all rows")
cfB_op = fit(ridgeB, -0.5, 0.5, "B operating window")

# calibration: anchor c_tg at the prior (single hBN dielectric, better constrained), set c_bg from the operating-window ratio
cf = cfA_op if cfA_op is not None else cfA_all
ratio = -cf[0]; c_tg = c_tg0; c_bg = ratio * c_tg
n0, _ = calc_nD(cf[1], 0.0, c_tg, c_bg); n_offset = -n0
nA_ridge = calc_nD(np.polyval(cf, ridgeA[:, 0]), ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0]
print(f"\nCALIBRATION (ridge A, operating window): ratio {ratio:.3f} (prior {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}, {100*(ratio/(c_bg0/c_tg0)-1):+.0f}%), "
      f"c_tg {c_tg:.3e} F/m2 (prior anchor), c_bg {c_bg:.3e}; n_offset {n_offset:+.4f}e12; closure max|n| on fitted line {np.abs(nA_ridge).max():.3f}e12")
nB = calc_nD(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0] if len(ridgeB) else np.array([np.nan])
print(f"ridge B density offset relative to A: n_B = {np.nanmedian(nB):+.3f}e12 (std {np.nanstd(nB):.3f}), i.e. region B is {'hole' if np.nanmedian(nB)>0 else 'electron'}-doped vs A by {abs(np.nanmedian(nB)):.2f}e12")
# D = 0 line of region A: V_tg = (c_bg/c_tg) V_bg + V_tg0 where n=0 at ... use calc_gate_voltages
ns = np.linspace(-1.5, 4.5, 601); Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, np.zeros_like(ns), c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
ok = (Vt >= -0.3) & (Vt <= 1.0) & (Vb >= -1.3) & (Vb <= 2.0)
print(f"D = 0 line (region A) realized n-window inside validators: {ns[ok].min():+.2f} .. {ns[ok].max():+.2f} e12; "
      f"CNP at (Vtg, Vbg) = ({calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[0]:+.3f}, {calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[1]:+.3f})")
# D range along ridge A
DA = calc_nD(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[1]
print(f"ridge A spans D = {DA.min():+.3f} .. {DA.max():+.3f} V/nm; peak R vs D: " +
      ", ".join(f"{d:+.2f}:{r:.0f}" for d, r in sorted(zip(np.round(DA, 2), ridgeA[:, 2]))[::6]))
json.dump({"run": rid, "ratio": ratio, "c_tg": c_tg, "c_bg": c_bg, "n_offset": n_offset, "D_offset": float(-D0_raw) if "D0_raw" in globals() else 0.0,
           "slope": cf[0], "intercept": cf[1], "window": "A |Vbg|<0.5", "nB_offset": float(np.nanmedian(nB))},
          open(Path(file_path).parent / "hera_scratch" / "cal_run5.json", "w"), indent=1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))
m = ax[0].pcolormesh(Vtg, Vbg, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax[0], label="log10 |Rxx| (Ohm)")
ax[0].plot(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], "c.", ms=3, label="ridge A pts"); ax[0].plot(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], "g.", ms=3, label="ridge B pts")
xx = np.array([Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()])
ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cf, xx), xx, "w--", lw=1, label=f"A fit (op. window): slope {cf[0]:+.3f}")
if cfB_all is not None: ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cfB_all, xx), xx, "g--", lw=1, label=f"B fit: slope {cfB_all[0]:+.3f}")
ax[0].plot(Vt[ok], Vb[ok], "y:", lw=1.5, label="D = 0 (calibrated)")
ax[0].set_xlim(Vtg.min(), Vtg.max()); ax[0].set_ylim(Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()); ax[0].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right"); ax[0].set_title(f"run {rid} gatemap — ridges + calibration")
# (n, D) projection
N, D = calc_nD(Vtg[None, :], Vbg[:, None], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
m2 = ax[1].pcolormesh(N, D, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m2, ax=ax[1], label="log10 |Rxx|")
ax[1].axhline(0, color="y", ls=":", lw=1); ax[1].set_xlabel("n (1e12 cm^-2)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("D (V/nm)"); ax[1].set_title("(n, D) projection, region-A calibration")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# D_offset from the CNP-resistance symmetry in ±D (ridge A only, n within 0.1e12 of the fit line)
rows = []
for i in range(g.nrows):
    vc = cf[0] * Vbg[i] + cf[1]
    if vc < Vtg.min() + 0.03 or vc > Vtg.max() - 0.03: continue
    msk = np.abs(Vtg - vc) < 0.12
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0); j = np.argmax(np.where(msk, r, -1))
    n_j, D_j = calc_nD(Vtg[j], Vbg[i], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
    if abs(n_j) < 0.1: rows.append((D_j, r[j]))
rows = np.array(sorted(rows)); k = np.argmin(rows[:, 1]); sel = np.abs(rows[:, 0] - rows[k, 0]) < 0.12
cq = np.polyfit(rows[sel, 0], rows[sel, 1], 2); D0_raw = -cq[1] / (2 * cq[0])
print(f"R_CNP(D) minimum: {rows[k,1]:.0f} Ohm at raw D = {rows[k,0]:+.3f}; parabola vertex raw D = {D0_raw:+.4f} V/nm -> D_offset = {-D0_raw:+.4f}")
plt.figure(figsize=(5, 3.5)); plt.plot(rows[:, 0], rows[:, 1], "o-", ms=3); plt.axvline(D0_raw, color="r", ls="--")
plt.xlabel("raw D (V/nm)"); plt.ylabel("R_CNP ridge A (Ohm)"); plt.title("CNP resistance vs D — vertex = physical D = 0"); plt.show()
```
# Tetralayer FS-count forward model — ABAB vs ABCA (vs ABCB)

Backs the `recipes/investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
This model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count**, the **Onsager
frequencies F(n)** (and vs interlayer potential u_D for ABCA), and the
**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m\*(n), both carrier signs. **ABAB** from the 2N-band SWMcC Hamiltonian (Koshino–McCann PRB 83, 165443 Eq. 1, N = 4), graphite parameters, via a rotationally-symmetric signed-density radial solve (electron pockets +k²/π, hole pockets −k²/π; the two bilayer-like blocks emerge automatically). **ABCA** from the 8-band continuum model of arXiv 2606.05356 S15 (Eqs. 8–14), parameter Set 1, on a 2D k-grid (trigonal warping → the low-density three-pocket → annulus → single Lifshitz cascade); interlayer potential u_D via the onsite U_l structure. **ABCB** qualitative, via the generic linkage builder. A generic `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` dispatches any stacking string ('ABAB','ABCA','ABA','ABC',…) to a Bernal / rhombohedral / mixed block builder by link sense, so trilayer sequences run for backtests. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k, positive/area-based for electron- and hole-like orbits alike. Pure numpy/scipy; `selftest()`/`__main__` runs every validation gate and prints the key tables. |

## API (call shapes)

- `abab_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, kF), ...])` — every ABAB Onsager orbit at
  E_F, sorted by F.
- `abab_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> [(F, m*/m_e), ...]` — per-orbit cyclotron masses,
  m\* = ℏ²k_F/|dE/dk|, same orbits/order as `abab_fs`.
- `abca_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, topo, n_components, n_freq, F_total)` — topology
  from connected components of the Fermi sea (single / annulus / k-pocket).
- `abca_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> (F_total, m*/m_e)` — from dn/dE_F on the same solve;
  pocket-summed in the cascade region.
- `abcb_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, ncomp), ...])` — **qualitative**, electron
  side only: the two low-energy conduction tones (cubic J = 3 + Dirac J = 1).
- Generic underneath: `bernal_fs`/`bernal_mstar`/`rhombo_fs`/`rhombo_mstar`
  take a sequence + `Params`; `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` returns the
  Hamiltonian; `ABAB`, `ABCA`, `ABA_TRI` are the parameter sets.

Masses are positive for electron- and hole-like orbits alike; the carrier sign
comes from the input n.

## Domain — loud, never clamped

The solvers raise `ValueError` (naming the covered range) for any density
outside the solved table; E_F rows whose Fermi contour would cross the k-grid
edge are excluded from the table on both sides. Solved coverage at u_D = 0:
ABAB ≈ −17.7…+17.1 ×10¹² cm⁻², ABCA ≈ ±11.5 ×10¹² cm⁻² — comfortably beyond
the ±8×10¹² cm⁻² design target.

## Parameters and validity

**Semi-quantitative — trust topology, shape, and partition, not absolute
frequencies.** The discriminating outputs are the FS count, the ABAB partition
and its φ²-split masses, and the model-independent Luttinger sum
Σ±f = (h/4e)|n|. Absolute frequencies inherit the hopping-parameter error bars.

- **ABAB**: Koshino–McCann graphite SWMcC set {γ₀ = 3.0, γ₁ = 0.4, γ₂ = −0.02,
  γ₄ = 0.04, γ₅ = 0.04, Δ′ = 0.05 eV}, all remote couplings ON. **γ₃ = 0**:
  the BL-contour trigonal warping is neglected so the solve stays radial (same
  precedent and caveat as the trilayer ABA treatment — γ₃ touches only the
  low-|n| BL fine structure). The 0.724 / 0.276 partition and φ² ≈ 2.618 mass
  ratio are the **low-n parabolic (decomposition) asymptote**; two effects
  distort them away from it — non-parabolicity (the bilayer bands bend toward
  linear) pulls the ratio *down* with rising |n|, while the γ₂-scale
  band-bottom offset dominates at low |n| and washes out with rising |n|. In
  the full model the electron-side partition passes through ≈ 0.73 near
  |n| ≈ 6×10¹²; the hole side runs lower (≈ 0.64) from the Δ′/γ₄ e–h asymmetry
  and the near-CNP semimetal overlap (§ below). Even-N has no mirror plane, so
  the two bilayer blocks are mixed by γ₂/γ₅ at the ~20 meV scale and inter-block
  magnetic breakdown is symmetry-allowed — the two-FS picture is exact only
  above that scale.
- **ABCA**: arXiv 2606.05356 S15 Set 1 {γ₀ = 3.1, γ₁ = 0.38, γ₂ = −0.015,
  γ₃ = 0.29, γ₄ = 0.141, δ = 0.0105, Δ₂ = 0.002 eV}, **γ₃ ON** (trigonal
  warping is the physics of the low-density cascade, not fine structure).
  u_D enters as a linear interlayer potential V_l = l·u_D (no Hartree screening).
  At operating density (|n| ≳ 2×10¹²) the pocket is single and F(n) is

This model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count**, the **Onsager
frequencies F(n)** (and vs interlayer potential u_D for ABCA), and the
**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m\*(n), both carrier signs. **ABAB** from the 2N-band SWMcC Hamiltonian (Koshino–McCann PRB 83, 165443 Eq. 1, N = 4), graphite parameters, via a rotationally-symmetric signed-density radial solve (electron pockets +k²/π, hole pockets −k²/π; the two bilayer-like blocks emerge automatically). **ABCA** from the 8-band continuum model of arXiv 2606.05356 S15 (Eqs. 8–14), parameter Set 1, on a 2D k-grid (trigonal warping → the low-density three-pocket → annulus → single Lifshitz cascade); interlayer potential u_D via the onsite U_l structure. **ABCB** qualitative, via the generic linkage builder. A generic `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` dispatches any stacking string ('ABAB','ABCA','ABA','ABC',…) to a Bernal / rhombohedral / mixed block builder by link sense, so trilayer sequences run for backtests. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k, positive/area-based for electron- and hole-like orbits alike. Pure numpy/scipy; `selftest()`/`__main__` runs every validation gate and prints the key tables. |

## API (call shapes)

- `abab_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, kF), ...])` — every ABAB Onsager orbit at
  E_F, sorted by F.
- `abab_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> [(F, m*/m_e), ...]` — per-orbit cyclotron masses,
  m\* = ℏ²k_F/|dE/dk|, same orbits/order as `abab_fs`.
- `abca_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, topo, n_components, n_freq, F_total)` — topology
  from connected components of the Fermi sea (single / annulus / k-pocket).
- `abca_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> (F_total, m*/m_e)` — from dn/dE_F on the same solve;
  pocket-summed in the cascade region.
- `abcb_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, ncomp), ...])` — **qualitative**, electron
  side only: the two low-energy conduction tones (cubic J = 3 + Dirac J = 1).
- Generic underneath: `bernal_fs`/`bernal_mstar`/`rhombo_fs`/`rhombo_mstar`

open_run (path: 'str | Path') -> 'Run'
    Open a sweep run directory — completed or in flight.
    
        `path` is the run dir (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Must contain
        `metadata.json` and either `data.tsv.gz` or `data.tsv`. Column names
        come from metadata — TSVs are headerless, and sweep writes `columns`
        to `metadata.json` at sweep start, so names resolve mid-run too. An
        in-flight run's TSV may end mid-row; only newline-terminated rows are
        trusted (sweep writes row-at-a-time, so interior lines are whole).

sdh_onset (R: 'np.ndarray', B: 'np.ndarray', *, b_hi: 'float | None' = None, b_lo: 'float' = 0.3, r_full_scale: 'float | None' = None, headroom: 'float' = 0.95, bg_degree: 'int' = 5, f_min: 'float' = 3.0, snr_threshold: 'float' = 5.0, n_periods: 'float' = 3.0, min_periods: 'float' = 2.0, step_frac: 'float' = 0.25, gap_widths: 'float' = 0.5, min_pts: 'int' = 8, max_tones: 'int' = 8, tone_floor_mult: 'float' = 4.0, marginal_mult: 'float' = 2.0) -> 'SdhOnset'
    Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single Rxx trace.
    
        `R` is one longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`, `B` the matching field
        `(n_B,)` (arbitrary spacing). Removes a degree-`bg_degree` B-space
        polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT
        scans (`_tone_id`), then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter from
        high B down to where it sinks into the record's white-noise floor
        (`_track_tone` — a 5σ-style statistical onset, which legitimately sits
        below a by-eye read).
    
        Returns an `SdhOnset`; `onset_b` is the minimum onset

    Per-column Shubnikov–de Haas FFT in 1/B.
    
        `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)` (rows = field, the `FanGrids` row axis); `B`
        is the per-row field `(n_B,)` — arbitrarily spaced. For each column:
        select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, remove a degree-
        `bg_degree` polynomial background in **B-space** (`None` skips), then take
        the FFT in 1/B. The background subtraction happens on the raw B axis
        *before* the 1/B step because the MR background is smooth in B, not 1/B.
    
        The 1/B resample is **conditional**. The field may be swept uniformly in
        1/B (then the samples a

field_invB (B_start: 'float', B_end: 'float', N: 'int') -> 'np.ndarray'
    Field axis of `N` points from `B_start` to `B_end`, uniform in 1/B.
    
        SdH oscillations are periodic in 1/B, so an FFT-bound field sweep samples
        evenly in 1/B (not in B). This is the measurement-side companion to
        `sdh_fft`'s uniform-1/B path: sweeping `field_invB` hands `sdh_fft` an
        already-even 1/B record (no resample). Argument order sets the sweep
        direction — high `B_start` descends, low `B_start` ascends.
    
        Both endpoints must be > 0 (1/B is taken). Returns `(N,)` Tesla.

luttinger_frequency (n: 'Any') -> 'np.ndarray'
    Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla.
    
        A single Fermi surface carrying the full density `n` gives this SdH
        frequency; the 4 is the spin×valley (4-fold) Landau degeneracy. `n` is in
        m^-2 (SI — feed `GateCalibration.density` output directly). Returns `|n|`
        form: the SdH frequency is positive for either carrier sign.

resistance_grids (fan: 'FanGrids', channels: 'list[str] | None' = None) -> 'ResistanceGrids'
    Per-channel resistance grids `R = (V/gain_V) / I` from a `FanGrids`.
    
        The denominator is the *measured* drain current `I = X_cur / gain_cur`
        (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a nominal bias
        current. Gains come from `measurement_config` (shared `resolve_channels`);
        nothing is hardcoded. Returned R is **signed** (X/I) — take `np.abs` for
        Rxx magnitude, keep the sign for Rxy/Hall. `channels` restricts the
        voltage channels returned (the current channel is always resolved).

fan_grids (run: "'str | Path | Run'", columns: 'list[str] | None' = None) -> 'FanGrids'
    Re-form a 2D fan into per-column grids, keeping only complete slow rows.
    
        `run` is a run directory or an already-loaded `Run`. `nfast` comes from
        metadata (never hardcoded); trailing rows of an in-progress sweep are
        dropped via `nrows = total // nfast`. `columns` restricts which columns
        are retained in `.data`/`.cols` (the reshape is unaffected).

resolve_channels (meta: 'dict[str, Any]', include: 'list[str] | None' = None) -> 'list[Channel]'
    Resolve the lock-in `_X` columns of a run into `Channel`s.
    
        Gains and role labels come from `meta['measurement_config']`. `include`,
        if given, restricts to those channel ids (e.g. ['sr1','sr2']) or column
        names. Handles both rig namings (`sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain`, `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`).

current_channel (channels: 'list[Channel]') -> 'Channel | None'
    The single transimpedance current channel, or None if not exactly one.
    
        The measured drain current (gain-divided) is the denominator of the
        four-probe resistance R = V / I — see `resistance_grids`.

"""Spot checks runs 6 (electron, n=+3.2e12) and 7 (hole, n=-1.2e12): raw MR, onset, FFT vs F_L + model."""
import sys, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency, SdhOnsetError
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.home() / "measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count"))

D = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data"
out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
runs = {6: (+3.2, 50e-6), 7: (-1.2, 50e-6)}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 11))
res = {}
for j, (rid, (n12, sens)) in enumerate(runs.items()):
    r = open_run(D / str(rid))
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); v = r.col("sr1_X"); i = r.col("sr0_X") / -1e6
    R = v / i
    Ibias = np.median(np.abs(i))
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, T = B[o], R[o], r.col("T_sample")[o]
    FL = float(luttinger_frequency(n12 * 1e16))
    print(f"=== run {rid}: n={n12:+.1f}e12  F_L={FL:.2f} T  pts={len(B)}  B {B.min():.3f}-{B.max():.3f}  "
          f"R {np.abs(R).min():.1f}-{np.abs(R).max():.1f} Ohm  I {Ibias*1e9:.2f} nA  "
          f"max|X|/sens={np.abs(v).max()/sens:.3f}  T {T.min():.3f}-{T.max():.3f}  "
          f"Ileak tg {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_tg_curr')).max():.2e} bg {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_bg_curr')).max():.2e}")
    ax[0, j].plot(B, R, lw=0.7); ax[0, j].set_title(f"run {rid} raw Rxx, n={n12:+.1f}e12"); ax[0, j].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[0, j].set_ylabel("R (Ohm)")
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(np.abs(R), B, r_full_scale=sens / Ibias)
        print(on.summary())
        res[rid] = on
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        print("SdhOnsetError:", e); on = None
    # background-subtracted
    m = B > 1.0
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], np.abs(R[m]), 5); dR = np.abs(R[m]) - np.polyval(cf, B[m])
    ax[1, j].plot(1 / B[m], dR, lw=0.6); ax[1, j].set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax[1, j].set_ylabel("dR (Ohm), deg-5 bg >1 T")
    if on is not None: ax[1, j].axvline(1 / on.onset_b, color="r", ls="--", label=f"onset {on.onset_b:.2f} T"); ax[1, j].legend()
    for lo in ([1.5, 2.0, 3.0] if on is None else sorted({max(on.onset_b, 1.0), 2.0, 3.0})):
        f, sp = sdh_fft(np.abs(R)[:, None], B, b_range=(lo, B.max()), bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=4096)
        ax[2, j].plot(f, sp[0] / sp[0][f > 2].max(), lw=0.8, label=f"window {lo:.2f}-{B.max():.1f} T")
        pk = [(f[k], sp[0][k]) for k in range(1, len(f) - 1) if sp[0][k] > sp[0][k-1] and sp[0][k] > sp[0][k+1] and f[k] > 2]
        pk = sorted(pk, key=lambda x: -x[1])[:6]
        print(f"  FFT {lo:.2f}-{B.max():.1f} T: dF={1/(1/lo-1/B.max()):.2f} T  peaks " + ", ".join(f"{a:.2f}({b/pk[0][1]:.2f})" for a, b in sorted(pk)))
    ax[2, j].axvline(FL, color="k", ls="--", label=f"F_L {FL:.1f}"); ax[2, j].set_xlim(0, 2.2 * FL); ax[2, j].legend(fontsize=7)
    ax[2, j].set_xlabel("F (T)")
    try:
        import fs_count_b0 as M
        ab = M.abab_fs(n12); am = M.abab_mstar(n12); ac = M.abca_fs(n12)
        print(f"  model ABAB tones: {[round(x[0],2) for x in ab[1]]}  m*: {[round(x[1],3) for x in am]}; ABCA F={ac[4]:.2f} topo={ac[1]}")
        for fz, _ in ab[1]: ax[2, j].axvline(abs(fz), color="b", ls=":", lw=0.8)
    except Exception as e:
        print("model err", e)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(out / "spot_runs67.png", dpi=90)

import sys, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.home() / "measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count"))
import fs_count_b0 as M

print("model table (u_D = 0):  n[1e12]  F_L | ABAB tones (m*) | ABCA F (m*)")
for n in (-1.27, -1.0, -0.7, -0.4, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.27):
    ab = M.abab_mstar(n * 1e16); Fa, ma = M.abca_mstar(n * 1e16)
    print(f"  {n:+5.2f}  {float(luttinger_frequency(n*1e16)):5.1f} | " + ", ".join(f"{F:.2f}({m:.3f})" for F, m in ab)
          + f" | {Fa:.2f} ({ma:.3f})")

D = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data"
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 8))
for j, (rid, n12, wins) in enumerate([(6, 3.2, [(1.0, 10), (1.5, 10), (2.0, 10), (1.0, 5.0), (5.0, 10)]),
                                     (7, -1.2, [(0.7, 10), (1.0, 10), (1.5, 10), (0.7, 3.0), (3.0, 10)])]):
    r = open_run(D / str(rid)); B = r.col("magnet_field"); R = np.abs(r.col("sr1_X") / (r.col("sr0_X") / -1e6))
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R = B[o], R[o]
    FL = float(luttinger_frequency(n12 * 1e16))
    for lo, hi in wins:
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(lo, hi), bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=1 << 15)
        s = sp[0]; sel = f > 1.5
        pk = [k for k in range(1, len(f) - 1) if s[k] > s[k - 1] and s[k] > s[k + 1] and f[k] > 1.5]
        pk = sorted(pk, key=lambda k: -s[k])[:7]
        print(f"run {rid} F_L={FL:.1f}  window {lo}-{hi} T (dF {1/(1/lo-1/hi):.2f} T): "
              + ", ".join(f"{f[k]:.2f}({s[k]/s[pk[0]]:.2f})" for k in sorted(pk)))
        if hi == 10:
            ax[0, j].plot(f, s / s[sel].max(), lw=0.8, label=f"{lo}-{hi} T")
    ax[0, j].axvline(FL, color="k", ls="--", label="F_L")
    for F, _ in M.abab_fs(n12 * 1e16)[1]: ax[0, j].axvline(F, color="b", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax[0, j].set_xlim(0, 2.5 * FL); ax[0, j].legend(fontsize=7); ax[0, j].set_title(f"run {rid} FFT (blue: ABAB model, k: F_L)")
    m = B > 0.7
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 7); ax[1, j].plot(1 / B[m], R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m]), lw=0.6)
    ax[1, j].set_xlabel("1/B"); ax[1, j].set_title(f"run {rid} dR (deg-7 bg in B, B>0.7 T)")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(Path(__file__).parent / "spot_runs67_fft.png", dpi=90)
# noise floor of run 6 at low B (1-2 T), residual rms
r = open_run(D / "6"); B = r.col("magnet_field"); R = np.abs(r.col("sr1_X") / (r.col("sr0_X") / -1e6))
m = (B > 1.0) & (B < 2.0); d = np.diff(R[m])
print(f"run 6 point-to-point noise 1-2 T: rms dR/sqrt2 = {np.std(d)/np.sqrt(2):.1f} Ohm; mean R {R[m].mean():.1f}")
r = open_run(D / "7"); B = r.col("magnet_field"); R = np.abs(r.col("sr1_X") / (r.col("sr0_X") / -1e6))

print(f"run 7 point-to-point noise 1-2 T: rms dR/sqrt2 = {np.std(d)/np.sqrt(2):.1f} Ohm")

89-
90-- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
91-- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
92-  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
93-  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
94-  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
95-  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
96-- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
97-  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
98-  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
99:- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
100-  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
101-  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
102-  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
103-  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
104:  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
105-- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
106-  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).
107-
108-All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
109-sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
110-`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).
111-

113-`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
114-id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

118-## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)
119-
120-- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
121-  without an explicit `basedir`.
122-- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
123-  basedir.
124-- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
125-- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
126-  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
127-  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
128-  monitor.

173-
174-Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
175:bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
176-these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

178-### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
179-The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
180-`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`

188-polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
189-`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

import numpy as np
import scipy.constants as cst
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from pathlib import Path

from hera.analysis import (
    open_run,
    plot_raw,
    summarize_run,
    fan_grids,
    resistance_grids,
    sdh_fft,
    GateCalibration,
    luttinger_frequency,
)

%matplotlib inline


def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


# Open a run by id: run(119) -> Run. Run.col(name) for a column;
# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))
```

## (n, D) — capacitance-based convention

`GateCalibration` carries the gate->(n, D) lever arm: `cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg)`
returns `n` in SI (m^-2; ×1e-16 for 10^12 cm^-2) and `D` in V/m. Build it from
the gate-stack thicknesses with `from_thicknesses` (κ_hBN/κ_SiO2 default).
This is the capacitance convention, **not** the toploader's `dtg/dbg` constant
form. Set `n_offset` / `D_offset` from `cnp-and-dline-calibration` once the CNP
/ D-line is live.

# slot: geometry — gate-stack thicknesses from the device card's Gate-stack

# Session gate calibration. cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg) -> (n [m^-2], D [V/m]);

## Runs 0–3 — gate C liveness: `gate-current-sanity-check` (B = 0, V_si = 0, T = 1.17 K)

**Read:** device alive on the provided contacts — drain current 9.86–9.94 nA (full 10 nA bias, R_2T ≪ 100 MΩ), Rxx(B_1−B_2) 60–330 Ω. No leakage: both gate currents stay at their pA offsets (BG +25 pA flat; TG −100 pA, drifting to 0 pA over V_tg = 0.4→1.0 V — a ~100 pA/0.6 V change, within the 2400's 1 µA-range offset behaviour and far below the 1 nA trip; watch it on the map, don't alarm). **Gate C: pass.** Two resistance maxima on each gate — TG: −0.21 V (322 Ω) and +0.11 V (244 Ω); BG: −0.26 V (302 Ω) and +0.14 V (273 Ω) — the same pair seen through both gates (position ratios 0.81 / 0.79 ≈ c_bg/c_tg; geometry prior 0.86). Two CNPs in series between B_1 and B_2 → two regions of different intrinsic doping (Δn ≈ 0.6×10¹² from the geometry prior), weak contrast (~3× over the metallic floor). Whether they are two flake domains or a contact-adjacent region is a gatemap question (parallel ridges vs not); series-mosaic is a stacking-read confound to carry forward.

    ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    V = r.col(r.swept_axis)
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = np.abs((r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I)
    i_tg, i_bg = r.col("k_2400_tg_curr"), r.col("k_2400_bg_curr")
    gate = r.swept_axis.replace("_volt", "")
    k = np.argmax(R); peaks[i] = (gate, V[k], R[k])
    print(f"run {i} {gate} {V[0]:+.2f}->{V[-1]:+.2f} V: R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm (max at {V[k]:+.3f} V), "
          f"I_drain {I.min()*1e9:.2f}-{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA, I_tg {i_tg.min()*1e12:+.0f}..{i_tg.max()*1e12:+.0f} pA, "
          f"I_bg {i_bg.min()*1e12:+.0f}..{i_bg.max()*1e12:+.0f} pA, T {r.col('T_sample').mean():.3f} K, interrupted={r.interrupted}")
    a = ax[0, 0] if "tg" in gate else ax[0, 1]
    a.plot(V, R, ".-", ms=3, label=f"run {i}"); a.set_xlabel(gate + " (V)"); a.set_ylabel("|Rxx| B_1-B_2 (Ohm)"); a.legend()
    b = ax[1, 0] if "tg" in gate else ax[1, 1]
    b.plot(V, i_tg * 1e12, ".-", ms=3, label=f"I_tg run {i}"); b.plot(V, i_bg * 1e12, ".-", ms=3, label=f"I_bg run {i}")
    b.set_xlabel(gate + " (V)"); b.set_ylabel("gate current (pA)"); b.legend(fontsize=7)
fig.suptitle("vti-02 gate C: gate-current-sanity-check, runs 0-3 (B = 0, Vsi = 0, other gate 0, T = 1.17 K)")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

"""sdh-spot-check read, runs 6 (electron, n = +3.2e12) and 7 (hole, n = -1.2e12), D = 0 (run-5 cal).
Raw MR first, then background-subtracted vs 1/B, sdh_onset per tone, windowed FFTs vs F_L and the ABAB model."""
import sys, warnings
from hera.analysis import sdh_onset, SdhOnsetError, resolve_channels
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.home() / "measurement_env" / "hera" / "models" / "tetralayer_fs_count"))
import fs_count_b0 as FSM

spots = {6: dict(n=+3.2, wins=[(1.0, 10.0), (1.5, 10.0), (2.0, 10.0)]),
         7: dict(n=-1.2, wins=[(0.7, 10.0), (1.0, 10.0), (1.5, 10.0)])}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 11))
for j, (rid, sp) in enumerate(spots.items()):
    r = run(rid); ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = np.abs((r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I); o = np.argsort(B); B, R, I = B[o], R[o], I[o]
    sens = 50e-6; FL = float(luttinger_frequency(sp["n"] * 1e16))
    ab = FSM.abab_mstar(sp["n"] * 1e16); Fa, ma = FSM.abca_mstar(sp["n"] * 1e16)
    print(f"=== run {rid}: n = {sp['n']:+.1f}e12, D = 0 | F_L = {FL:.1f} T | model ABAB " + ", ".join(f"{F:.1f} T (m* {m:.3f})" for F, m in ab)
          + f" | ABCA {Fa:.1f} T (m* {ma:.3f})")
    print(f"    B {B.min():.2f}-{B.max():.2f} T, {len(B)} pts; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; I {np.median(I)*1e9:.2f} nA; "
          f"peak |sr1_X|/FS = {np.abs(r.col('sr1_X')).max()/sens:.2f}; T {r.col('T_sample').min():.3f}-{r.col('T_sample').max():.3f} K; "
          f"max |I_tg|, |I_bg| = {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_tg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f}, {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_bg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f} pA")
    ax[0, j].plot(B, R, lw=0.7); ax[0, j].set(xlabel="B (T)", ylabel="|Rxx| B_1-B_2 (Ohm)", title=f"run {rid} RAW, n = {sp['n']:+.1f}e12, D = 0")
    # onset on the adequately sampled record (run 6 is 50 mT-sampled below 1 T: Nyquist-blind to F > ~7 T there)
    blo = 1.0 if rid == 6 else 0.3
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        try:
            on = sdh_onset(R, B, b_lo=blo, r_full_scale=sens / np.median(I)); print(on.summary())
        except SdhOnsetError as e:
            on = None; print("SdhOnsetError:", e)
    for x in w: print("    note:", str(x.message)[:160])
    m = B > 0.7
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 7)
    ax[1, j].plot(1 / B[m], R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m]), lw=0.6)
    ax[1, j].set(xlabel="1/B (1/T)", ylabel="dR (Ohm), deg-7 bg in B", title=f"run {rid} background-subtracted (B > 0.7 T)")
    for lo, hi in sp["wins"]:
        f, S = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(lo, hi), bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=1 << 14)
        s = S[0]; pk = [k for k in range(1, len(f) - 1) if s[k] > s[k - 1] and s[k] > s[k + 1] and f[k] > 1.5]
        pk = sorted(sorted(pk, key=lambda k: -s[k])[:6])
        print(f"    FFT {lo}-{hi} T (dF = {1/(1/lo-1/hi):.2f} T): " + ", ".join(f"{f[k]:.1f}({s[k]/max(s[pk]):.2f})" for k in pk))
        ax[2, j].plot(f, s / s[f > 1.5].max(), lw=0.9, label=f"{lo}-{hi} T")
    ax[2, j].axvline(FL, color="k", ls="--", label=f"F_L {FL:.1f} T")
    for F, _ in ab: ax[2, j].axvline(F, color="b", ls=":", lw=1)

## Runs 6–7 — SdH spot checks (`sdh-spot-check`), D = 0, electron n = +3.2×10¹² and hole n = −1.2×10¹²

Both complete (not interrupted), no leakage (≤ 0.2 nA), T 1.17–1.29 K, `sr1` peak ≤ 12 % of the 50 µV full scale (no clipping). Raw first, then background-subtracted, then per-tone onsets (`sdh_onset`) and windowed FFTs against F_L and the ABAB model (scale 1).

**Electron, run 6 (F_L = 33.1 T; ABAB model 7.3 / 25.8 T, ABCA 33.1 T).** Strong SdH above ~1.3 T that goes into the QH regime above ~5 T. Rxx minima reach 0 and slightly negative, so the B_1–B_2 pair has a small Hall admixture. Tones: **≈ 7.2 T** (SNR 100–120; still above threshold at the 1.0 T edge of the 10 mT-sampled record, so **its onset is below 1 T**. Run 6 is 50 mT-sampled below 1 T, which is blind to F ≳ 7 T there.) Also **≈ 22.3 T** (onset 1.4 T), **≈ 29.4 T** (onset 1.8 T), ≈ 14.8 T, and high-field-only combs at 39–118 T (onset ≥ 2.6 T; QH harmonics). `sdh_onset`'s ratio screen flags 14.8 / 22.3 / 29.4 as 2× / 3× / 4× of 7.2. The investigation forbids settling that on the ratio alone. 7.2 + 22.3 = 29.5 ≈ the 29.4 tone, so the same set reads as an ABAB pair at density scale ≈ 0.87–0.9 (model 7.3 / 25.8 → 6.4–6.6 / 22.4–23.2) plus a sum/breakdown tone at the F_L position. It also reads as a 7.2 T harmonic comb, or as an ABCA singleton at scale 0.89 with extras. **One density cannot separate these. The n-dependence can:** a harmonic tracks k·f₁(n), a real pocket tracks its own Onsager curve, and a sum tone tracks f₁ + f₂. That is the fan's job.

**Hole, run 7 (F_L = 12.4 T; ABAB model ≈ 6.0 / 6.6 T, ABCA 12.4 T at m* ≈ 1.1).** This side is cleaner: onset 0.7 T. Tones ≈ 6.6 T (dominant), ≈ 4.7 T, ≈ 12.3 T (strongest above 3 T), and ≈ 8.5 T. These sit in the investigation's **near-CNP hole exception regime**: on the D = 0 line the hole side is TG-limited at |n| ≤ 1.27×10¹². There the ABAB pair is close and balanced, and the 12.3 T tone could be F_L, 2 × 6.6 or a sum tone. **Not decisive.**

**Take:** the hole side is cleaner at its one density, but only the **electron side** reaches the |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹² band where the templates separate, and it carries SNR 50–120 tones there. The fan goes on the electron side. Onset inputs: the light tone is below 1 T (censored at the record edge), the heavy tones are at 1.4–1.8 T. The sensitivity (50 µV) and settling (10 τ) are inherited.

import numpy as np, json, sys
from pathlib import Path
from hera.analysis import field_invB, luttinger_frequency
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.home()/"measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count")); import fs_count_b0 as M
c = json.load(open("hera_scratch/cal_run5.json"))
n_lo, n_hi, N_n = 1.4, 3.2, 61
B_lo, B_hi = 0.8, 5.0
FLmax = float(luttinger_frequency(n_hi*1e16))
dinv_target = 1/(3*FLmax)
N_B = int(np.ceil((1/B_lo-1/B_hi)/dinv_target))+1
Bv = field_invB(B_lo, B_hi, N_B); dinv = 1/Bv[0]-1/Bv[1]
print(f"F_L(n_hi) {FLmax:.2f} T; N_B {N_B}; d(1/B) {dinv:.5f} -> {1/(dinv*FLmax):.2f} samples/period at F_L, {1/(dinv*FLmax*1.1):.2f} at scale 1.1; Nyquist f {1/(2*dinv):.1f} T")
ns = np.linspace(n_lo, n_hi, N_n); dn = ns[1]-ns[0]
LL = lambda B: 4*1.602176634e-19*B/6.62607015e-34/1e16
print(f"dn {dn:.4f}e12; LL spacing at B_lo {LL(B_lo):.4f}e12 -> {LL(B_lo)/dn:.2f} pts/LL; at 1 T {LL(1)/dn:.2f}")
Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, np.zeros_like(ns), c["c_tg"], c["c_bg"], c["n_offset"], c["D_offset"])
print(f"Vtg {Vt.min():+.4f}..{Vt.max():+.4f}  Vbg {Vb.min():+.4f}..{Vb.max():+.4f}")
# record / resolution
for blo_t in (B_lo, 1.4, 1.8):
    print(f"record above {blo_t} T: dF = {1/(1/blo_t-1/B_hi):.2f} T")
for n in (2.0, 2.2, 2.5, 2.8, 3.2):
    ab = M.abab_fs(n*1e16)[1]; f1 = ab[0][0]; FL=float(luttinger_frequency(n*1e16))
    print(f"n {n}: F_L {FL:.1f}; ABAB {[round(x[0],1) for x in ab]}; partner periods over [B_lo,B_hi] at scale 1/0.88: {f1*(1/B_lo-1/B_hi):.1f}/{0.88*f1*(1/B_lo-1/B_hi):.1f}; heavy-vs-F_L split {FL-ab[-1][0]:.1f} T")
# pricing
t_pt = 2.1 + 0.13
rows_t = N_n*t_pt + 2.0 + 1.5 + 3.0     # slow_delay + flyback + settle
ramp = (B_hi-B_lo)/0.137*60
pre = B_lo/0.137*60 + 40
tot = N_B*rows_t + ramp + pre
print(f"row {rows_t:.0f} s (+ramp); grid {N_B*rows_t/3600:.2f} h; in-fan ramp {ramp/60:.1f} min; pre-position {pre/60:.1f} min; total {tot/3600:.2f} h; x1.07 {1.07*tot/3600:.2f} h")
# cumulative time to row k
cum = np.cumsum([rows_t + abs(Bv[k]-Bv[k-1])/0.137*60 if k else rows_t for k in range(N_B)]) + pre
for Bc in (1.0, 1.5, 2.5, 4.0):
    k = np.argmin(abs(Bv-Bc)); print(f"B={Bc}: row {k}, t = {cum[k]/3600:.2f} h")
EOF

# === Landau fan, electron side, D = 0 (`landau-fan-vti`, for tetralayer-stacking-fs-count Step 4) ===
# n 1.4 -> 3.2e12 (61 pts, fast, paired Vtg/Vbg), B 0.8 -> 5.0 T uniform in 1/B (106 rows, slow, ascending)
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD
# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
N_LO, N_HI, N_N, D0 = 1.4, 3.2, 61, 0.0          # 1e12 cm^-2, V/nm
B_LO, B_HI, N_B = 0.8, 5.0, 106                    # T; d(1/B) = 0.0100 1/T = 1/(3 F_L(3.2e12))
ns = np.linspace(N_LO, N_HI, N_N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(N_N)
Vtgs, Vbgs = calc_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
Vtgs, Vbgs = np.asarray(Vtgs, float), np.asarray(Vbgs, float)
assert Vtgs.min() >= TG_MIN and Vtgs.max() <= TG_MAX and Vbgs.min() >= BG_MIN and Vbgs.max() <= BG_MAX, (Vtgs, Vbgs)
B_vec = field_invB(B_LO, B_HI, N_B)
assert B_vec.min() > 0 and B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP and np.all(np.diff(B_vec) > 0)
dinv = 1 / B_vec[0] - 1 / B_vec[1]
print(f"fast: n {ns[0]:+.2f}..{ns[-1]:+.2f}e12 ({N_N} pts, dn {ns[1]-ns[0]:.3f}e12), D = {D0}; Vtg {Vtgs[0]:+.4f}..{Vtgs[-1]:+.4f}, Vbg {Vbgs[0]:+.4f}..{Vbgs[-1]:+.4f} V")
print(f"slow: B {B_vec[0]:.3f} -> {B_vec[-1]:.3f} T, {N_B} rows uniform 1/B, d(1/B) = {dinv:.5f} 1/T (Nyquist {1/(2*dinv):.1f} T; F_L(3.2e12) = 33.1 T)")
# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---

One density reads this three ways: an ABAB pair at density scale ≈ 0.88 plus a sum/breakdown tone at the F_L position, a 7.2 T harmonic comb, or an ABCA singleton plus extras.
